subject: Post-call: NexaHealth integration & model-routing requirements
thread_summary: Post-call recap for NexaHealth covering SDK auth, routing policy needs (latency/cost/fallback), structured output/tool-calling, embeddings & reranker recommendations; includes SOW and architecture diagram; next steps: technical deep-dive + DocuSign.

Subject: Post-call recap: integration & model-routing requirements

Thanks again for the time today, Elena — great conversation. Summary and next steps below.

TL;DR: NexaHealth wants an inference integration for patient triage + knowledge search (embeddings + reranker) with predictable latency and cost controls; needs an auth story and regional routing (US).

Key notes from the call:
- Primary use cases: 1) patient triage (structured output + tool calling to update triage state), 2) knowledge search across internal KB (embeddings + reranker), 3) short-form summarization for clinical notes.
- Latency SLO: target 150-200ms median for triage fast-path; cost sensitivity for large batch rerank workflows.
- Data residency: US-only for PHI/PII workloads; non-PHI can route elsewhere.
- Compliance ask: SOC2 evidence + audit log retention options.

Integration asks for us:
- SDK auth options (API Key vs SSO) — please confirm preferred initial approach.
- Expected QPS and typical sequence length for triage prompts (tokens).
- Whether reranker must run on every query or only on a top-k shortlist.

Attachments: initial architecture diagram (nexa_architecture_v1.png) and SOW draft to follow.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (30-45 min) with engineering + solutions — propose Wed 7/29 or Thu 7/30.
2) We’ll circulate a draft SOW and architecture diagram (attached in next email).
3) Dev asks: send sample payloads and expected volumes.

If that matches your notes, reply with preferred auth and deep-dive time.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: integration & model-routing requirements — SDK & routing notes

Thanks, Elena — confirming Wed 7/29 10:00am PT works for us. Quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive so we can make the meeting productive:

Auth & SDK setup (recommended starter flow):
- API Key (short-term): store keys in your vault; Redwood SDK supports key rotation via header X-Redwood-Key.
- Long-term: OIDC / SAML SSO + mTLS for Private deployments (if you want KMS/HSM integration later).

Example (Node SDK) — minimal auth + streaming:

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.NEXA_RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-east-1' });
const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-chat-medium', input: 'Triage: patient symptoms...' });

Notes on routing & policy configuration:
- Policy constructs we recommend: priority-based routing (latency-first vs cost-first), fallback chains, and region pinning.
- Example policy: triage-route = [rw-chat-highperf@us-east-1 (latency target 150ms), rw-chat-cost@us-east-1 (fallback, 1/3 tokens cost), rw-chat-cost@us-west-2 (secondary fallback, lower cost)].
- Implement autoscaling + burst pools for triage fast-path; prefer continuous batching for bulk rerank jobs.

Structured output / tool calling:
- Use Redwood's structured-output schema to validate triage responses; use tool-calling hooks for state changes (e.g., POST to your triage service).
- For sensitive fields, redact at SDK layer and mark outputs for audit logging.

Embeddings + reranker pattern:
- Ingest KB -> dense embeddings (384-1536 dims). Use ANN index (FAISS/HNSW) for top-K (k=50) retrieval.
- Cross-encoder reranker only on top-10 to reduce cost — use a small cross-encoder tuned for precision.
- Cache embeddings + prefix KV cache for common queries.

Questions for Nexa before the deep-dive:
1) Expected QPS (triage vs search) and average tokens per request (prompt + response).
2) Do you expect synchronous rerank on all queries or async background refresh?
3) Any specific regulatory controls beyond SOC2 (e.g., audit retention days)?

I'll prepare a short routing-policy draft and a sample SDK integration repo to demo in the call.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: recommendations for embeddings & reranker

Elena — quick recommendations building on Dev's notes:  

- Embedding dims & index: start with 1024-d embeddings with HNSW for ANN; reduces retrieval latency and maintains quality.
- Reranker strategy: candidate fetch (top-50) -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank on top-10. Limit reranker to business hours for high-volume queries or run an L2 cache for frequent queries.
- Quantization: for your Dedicated/private footprint, 4-bit quantized models for reranker can cut cost ~2-3x with negligible perf loss.

Routing & policy templates (examples we’ll bring to the deep-dive):
- Latency-first policy: prefer high-perf model in us-east-1 with immediate fallback to cost model within same region.
- Cost-cap policy: if per-minute token spend > $X, move non-critical traffic to cost-optimized models and queue large batch reranks.
- Region pinning: PHI routes only within specified region pool; non-PHI can load-balance globally.

Operational suggestions:
- Canary rollout for model changes (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automated quality/regression checks (we can tie to your eval prompt set).
- Add a short eval harness for triage prompts to detect quality regressions before model switch.

I’ll attach the routing-policy draft and small examples in the repo for the call.

Neha
